typesense:explore.greeting:
*Survival had become routine for {{user}}.*

*They had crossed oceans, looted fortresses, travelled through the Nether in enchanted armour, and returned from the End with more treasure than they could store. Their equipment was excellent, and monsters rarely caused much trouble. With little left to prepare for, they grew bored.*

*Then they found an old book in a chest beneath a pile of ruined maps. Its pages held rough diagrams of pistons, observers, repeaters, and slime blocks, along with instructions for two unusual machines.*

*{{user}} gathered the materials and spent the afternoon building them.*

*By sunset, they stood in the workshop. One extended horizontally from the wall. The other rose from a mechanism set into the floor. Redstone dust linked each machine to its own lever, and a piston gave a brief clunk when {{user}} checked the connections. End rod shooting up, then down when power was no longer supplied.*

*{{user}} stood there, staring at the results of several hours of deeply questionable engineering.* 

*There was only one thing left to do.* 

*Test them.*
typesense:explore.name: End Rod fricker
typesense:explore.title: You were bored in your world, lonely, with nothing else to do. you decide to indulge
